# S262 — Running view: only the tabs that fit it, and jump to it after a wave launch

*Proposed.* While the Running sidebar entry is selected, the view bar shows only the tabs that fit it: `Overview (Running)` and Questions, as the owner proposed. A wave launch from the Waves screen that the daemon accepts moves the owner to the Running entry with the new run's row selected, unless the spec check still holds a ticked item for questions. This is TUI only: nothing here touches `internal/engine`, `internal/daemon` or `cmd`. The exact tab set, the jump rule and the flows it covers wait on the owner questions at the end; everything else is written in full.

**Findings:** Owner 2026-11-03 (screenshots of the Running entry and of a Waves launch): (1) With Running selected the view bar still shows Questions, Waves, Roadmap and Decisions as cross-project views (S140; docs/dashboard.md:295). Proposed: while Running is selected show only Overview (Running) and Questions (a paused run asks there); hide Waves, Roadmap and Decisions. Waves asks the daemon for every project's suggestion, so it is also the costly one. This reverses part of S140. (2) After l on the Waves screen the TUI stays put: the only sign is a footer status (launched N items; enter on a running row opens its run, internal/tui/waves.go:~443-452), and the owner reported it looked like it went nowhere (a slicer wave of four items ended after its spec check; ork status then showed no run for slicer; the footer text was not seen, so the cause is unverified). Proposed: after the daemon accepts the launch, jump to the Running entry with the new run's row selected; do not jump while the spec check holds an item for questions, because those are answered on the Waves screen (pending: spec.check). Open owner questions: which tabs to keep on Running, what the jump selects when several items launch, how the owner gets back to the Waves composer (esc or the sidebar), and whether a held launch should say so in a banner. A ui.* adj key and docs/dashboard.md change; UI pass applies. Related: S140, S82, S190, S251. · **Size:** M · **Tree:**

**2026-11-03** — Owner answers 2026-11-03 (interactive): Q1 and Q2 the Running entry shows Overview (Running) and Questions only; Questions lists every project as on Needs you; no keys to hidden tabs; the combined Waves and Roadmap code is deleted (Q2b). This reverses adj 121 ui.view-list for Running and the S140 owner decision of 2026-10-27. Q3 and Q5 as written: jump to Running with the first launched run selected when every item is accepted; stay on Waves on any item error, after leaving Waves, or while an item is held for spec questions; also after a single-item Roadmap launch; never after retry, answer, approve or fix. All remaining recommendations accepted (Q4 no new key, Q6 no banner, Q7 adj records ui.running-tabs and ui.launch-jump with --ref S262, left for the owner's later pass). ## Why

Owner request, 2026-11-03 (screenshots of the Running entry and of a Waves launch).

Part 1, the tabs. With Running selected the view bar still shows Questions, Waves, Roadmap and Decisions, each as a cross-project view (S140, owner decision 2026-10-27 in the S140 spec; `docs/dashboard.md:295-306`). The owner thinks the Running view does not need them. What the code at HEAD of main (a7ae6fc) does:

- The view bar is one fixed list of five views, each with a `built` flag (`internal/tui/view.go:479-491`). `viewBarCount` draws every view and only renames the first to `Overview (Running)` while Running is selected (`view.go:499-540`, the rename at `:511-513`). `moveView` cycles every built view (`internal/tui/model.go:1304-1325`). Nothing hides a view per sidebar entry.
- `switchTo` changes the sidebar entry and keeps `m.view` (`model.go:1095-1119`). So an owner on a project's Waves who presses `[` to reach Running lands on the combined Waves.
- The combined tabs are S140 code that only the Running entry reaches: `openAllWaves` asks the daemon for every project's suggestion, one call after the other (`internal/tui/waves.go:84-88`, `:110-140`; the `aggregate` flag and `groups` at `waves.go:26-29`, used at `:153`, `:392`, `:661`, `:752`, `:903`, `internal/tui/keys.go:444`, `internal/tui/lineup.go:39`). The combined Roadmap is `runningRoadmapItems` and `runningRoadmapView` (`internal/tui/overview.go:1765-1848`), reached from `internal/tui/roadmap.go:116-118` and `:224-226`. Questions and Decisions with an aggregate entry use the same all-projects code as Needs you (`dashboard.md:295-298`), so they do not depend on Running.
- At 80 columns the five-tab bar does not fit beside the sidebar, so the Questions count is dropped (`view.go:312-321`; `docs/dashboard.md:1153-1155` names `Overview (Running)` at 80 columns as the example). With two tabs the count fits again.
- S140's later notes on the combined Waves (projects not loaded are left out, calls are serial, error lines are plain) are moot if the combined Waves goes.

Part 2, the launch. After `l` and `y` on the Waves screen the TUI stays on Waves. `applyWaves` for kind `start` (`waves.go:417-487`) marks each launched item `[>]` with `running RUN`, unticks it, and sets the status line to `launched ID as RUN; enter opens it` or `launched N items; enter on a running row opens its run` (`waves.go:443-449`). Ticked items that were not in the call wait on spec questions and stay ticked; the status adds `ID waits on spec questions` (`waves.go:460-476`). `enter` on a launched row sets `m.view = 0` and selects the run through `jumpRun` and `selectJumpRun` (`waves.go:860-871`, `:911-916`), on the project's own Overview, not on Running. The owner reported that the launch looked like it went nowhere. The owner's own account says the footer text was not seen, so whether the status line was there is not verified.

The pieces for a jump exist: `jumpRun` survives until a snapshot shows the run (`model.go:1214`, `TestWavesJumpWaitsForSnapshot`, `internal/tui/waves_test.go:1124`) and any navigation key clears it (`model.go:607-611`). A launched engine run in state `queued` or any active state is in the Running section (`internal/source/source.go:310-326`). Leaving the Waves view drops the composer (`dropWaves` through `openWaves`, `waves.go:77-88`), so the ticks of a held item are lost on any jump. That is why the jump must not happen while an item is held: its questions are answered on the Waves screen (`docs/dashboard.md:1311-1317`).

Single-item launch: the Roadmap launch (`internal/tui/launch.go:208-250`) shows `ork run P ID: done` and stays on the Roadmap; it drops the run record that `run.start` returns (`launch.go:229`; the record is returned at `internal/daemon/runs.go:590-592`). Retry is `t`, not `r` (`r` is refresh, `internal/tui/keys.go:93`, `:125`); `t`, answer, approve and fix act on a run that is already on the screen.

Checks made:

- slicer provides nothing like it: `slicer --root ../slicer find "launch jump"` and `find "view bar"` print `no matching items`.
- In ork, S66 (mouse: click tabs) is open and would click only the tabs drawn. S264 (spec check progress in launch) also edits `internal/tui/waves.go`, `internal/tui/launch.go` and the Waves section of `docs/dashboard.md`, so the two must not share a wave; land one first. S82 (Waves screen), S190 (TUI notes sweep T2) and S251 (settings pane) are done or do not touch the view bar or the start reply.
- adj: `ui.view-list` (#121, decided `five-views`: "tab and shift+tab skip views not built yet and the bar shows them dim") is the record this reverses for the Running entry. `ui.sidebar-running` (#169) and `ui.views` (#120) stand as they are. `ui.project-keys` (#160) is unchanged. The S140 decision of 2026-10-27 is in the S140 spec only, not in adj. `ui.running-tabs` and `ui.launch-jump`: not found.

UI slice: rule u10 applies (UI pass, r14). Layouts are checked at 80x24 and 100x30.

## Open owner questions

The spec waits on these. Each has a recommendation; no adj record decides them yet.

- Q1. Which tabs stay while Running is selected? (a) `Overview (Running)` and Questions, as proposed; Questions keeps listing every project's questions, engine and adj, as on Needs you. (b) The same two, with Questions narrowed to the questions of runs (no adj records): a new filter and its tests. (c) `Overview (Running)` only: the bar has one tab and `tab` does nothing there. (d) Overview, Questions and Decisions. Recommendation: (a), the smallest change that matches the request; a paused run's question is there. Steps 2, 3, 7 and the tab tests wait on this.
- Q2. (a) Which keys reach the hidden tabs from Running? Options: none (select Needs you or a project; Needs you already shows Questions and Decisions for all projects), or keep `tab` cycling into them while the bar hides them. Recommendation: none; a tab that the bar does not show is a surprise. (b) The combined Waves and Roadmap code becomes unreachable: remove it (fewer lines, five tests deleted, S140's later notes on the combined Waves retired) or keep it (smaller diff, dead code). Recommendation: remove, in this slice. Steps 3 and 4 wait on this.
- Q3. The jump rule. (a) Several items launch: select the first launched run in the reply's order (recommended), or the top Running row, or open every new run with `space`. (b) Some items fail admission and others launch: stay on Waves so the failures can be read and re-ticked there (recommended), or jump and keep the errors on the status line. (c) The owner left the Waves screen before the reply: no jump (recommended), or jump anyway. (d) A held item: no jump, as the owner said (written that way). (e) `enter` on a launched row of a held launch: keep today's project Overview (recommended), or go to Running too. Steps 5 and 6 wait on this.
- Q4. How does the owner get back to the Waves composer? (a) No new key: the project's digit or `]`, then `tab`; the composer reloads and nothing is lost, because a jump only happens when nothing is held (recommended). (b) `esc` once on Running right after a jump goes back to that project's Waves: hidden one-shot state, and `esc` already closes panes, help and the status. (c) The status text also names the way back (the project's digit, then `tab`): the line then passes 80 columns when it carries a run ID. Step 6 waits on this.
- Q5. Does the jump also apply elsewhere? (a) The single-item Roadmap launch (`launch.go`): needs the `run.start` record kept, the status changes from `ork run P ID: done` to `launched ID as RUN; enter opens it`, and two existing tests change. (b) `t` retry, answer, approve and fix: the run is already on the screen where the owner acted. Recommendation: (a) yes, for the same reason as the wave; (b) no. Step 8 waits on this.
- Q6. Does a held launch get a banner on the Waves screen? Today the held row says `waits on N spec questions`, the status ends `ID waits on spec questions` and the hint reads `l answer spec questions`.
